system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime

- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side Review of Seller SPA Update & Disclosure Letter

**Preliminary note on the Seller's framing.** The preamble asserting that these positions are "market", "settled at principal level" and "FINAL" is unverified Seller advocacy, not a record of any agreement I can confirm. Unless the Wattlebridge deal team confirms a principal-level agreement in writing, treat every position as open. Also note the Disclosure Letter itself contradicts the Update draft on several points (Bluefen, Riverlark, bonuses) – the Letter admits gaps the Update glosses over. Use the Letter against the Update.

**Aggregate exposure check.** Known/quantified issues already on the table: Riverlark ~AUD 3.2m, bonuses AUD 420k (+ on-costs), Ironquay AUD 180k (+ IP risk), Sandbar AUD 330k, plus an unquantified privacy incident and a 30%-of-revenue consent at risk. That is >AUD 4.1m before any unknowns – against a proposed general cap of AUD 4.8m. The limitation package is not fit for this risk profile.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- Seller: 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- Buyer wants: 50% of price minimum (AUD 12m) for general warranties; separate 100% cap for fundamental/title/tax; specific indemnities outside the cap.
- Recommendation: Reject 20%; counter at 50% with carve-outs. *Reason: known exposures already approach the proposed cap, leaving no cover for undisclosed matters.*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket**
- Seller: AUD 25k per claim; AUD 250k basket; excess-only recovery.
- Buyer wants: AUD 10k de minimis (related claims aggregated); AUD 120–240k basket (0.5–1%) on a tipping ("first-dollar") basis; no basket for fundamental, tax or specific indemnity claims.
- Recommendation: Counter at AUD 10k / AUD 150k tipping. *Reason: an excess-only basket plus a high de minimis means the Buyer self-insures the first ~AUD 275k+ of every category of breach.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- Seller: 18 months from Completion; "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated".
- Buyer wants: 24 months for general warranties (covers two audit cycles); 7 years tax; fundamental/title unlimited or statutory limitation; claims notified in time survive until resolved.
- Recommendation: Counter at 24 months and strike the "applies to all Claims" default. *Reason: 18 months may expire before the second post-Completion audit surfaces accounting or revenue-recognition issues.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime**
- Seller: Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties.
- Buyer wants: Fundamental warranties (title, capacity, authority, no encumbrances) capped at 100% of price, 6–7 year limitation, outside basket/de minimis.
- Recommendation: Reject outright. *Reason: "administrative simplicity" is no justification for limiting recovery if the Buyer does not actually acquire clean title to what it paid AUD 24m for.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- Seller: Limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions "apply to all Claims of any nature" – no fraud carve-out.
- Buyer wants: Express carve-out from all caps, thresholds, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, fraudulent misrepresentation, wilful concealment and wilful default by the Seller or its officers.
- Recommendation: Non-negotiable insertion. *Reason: limiting liability for fraud is contrary to public policy and the clause would also be unenforceable in part under NSW law – its presence signals aggressive drafting.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- Seller: General disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- Buyer wants: Only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter"; specific disclosures only; no general data room or public register disclosure (ASIC/PPSR/IP Australia searches disclosed only if actually annexed).
- Recommendation: Reject general disclosure; require specific, cross-referenced disclosures against numbered warranties. *Reason: a general data room dump would neutralise most warranties, and the Letter's own §1.4 refuses to admit anything.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- Seller: No claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers "had knowledge" of, including anything "discoverable" from data room or public records.
- Buyer wants: Deletion. Fallback: limited to actual knowledge of 2–3 named deal team members on Completion of a matter constituting a breach, excluding advisers and constructive/discoverable knowledge.
- Recommendation: Delete. *Reason: "discoverable" imports constructive knowledge of everything in the data room and public registers, effectively re-creating general disclosure through the back door.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- Seller: "Reasonable endeavours"; condition treated as satisfied on delivery of counterparty's written consent. Disclosure Letter §2 admits no consent and no evidence the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- Buyer wants: Unconditional, unqualified written consent **and** evidence the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied as a Condition Precedent; Seller to use best/all reasonable endeavours; Buyer-only waiver right; termination right if not satisfied by Long Stop Date; alternatively price retention/escrow referable to Bluefen revenue.
- Recommendation: Hard CP, Buyer waiver only. *Reason: Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue – a consent delivered subject to unsatisfied conditions is no consent.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- Seller: Release "to be provided following Completion". Letter §3 admits not repaid, no discharge.
- Buyer wants: Repayment at Completion from the purchase price via funds flow (deduction consistent with debt-free/cash-free baseline); executed payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge delivered at Completion as a Completion deliverable; Riverlark change-of-control waiver obtained pre-Completion.
- Recommendation: Reject post-Completion release; make it a Completion deliverable with price deduction. *Reason: AUD 3.2m secured debt surviving Completion breaches the debt-free baseline and leaves the Company in default under clause 8.1 change-of-control.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- Seller: AUD 420k closing bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised in funds flow. Letter §5 admits exclusion and silence on on-costs.
- Buyer wants: Bonuses plus superannuation, payroll tax and on-costs (budget ~AUD 500k+) treated as Transaction Expenses / Indebtedness deducted from the price in the funds flow; or paid by Seller pre-Completion with evidence; specific indemnity for any shortfall.
- Recommendation: Price deduction in funds flow plus specific indemnity. *Reason: these are Completion-triggered liabilities of the Company that would otherwise land on the Buyer post-Completion.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- Seller: Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment (AUD 180k); "adequate". Letter §4 admits no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment.
- Buyer wants: CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared SOW3 payment plus executed confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay covering all SOW Project Materials; indemnity extended to all loss from non-transfer of any Ironquay IP (including re-development costs, third-party claims, loss of revenue), uncapped or separate cap, outside basket.
- Recommendation: Expand indemnity and add deliverable. *Reason: under clause 7.3 the Company does not own the SOW3 IP until paid – the risk is loss of core IP, not an AUD 180k invoice.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- Seller: "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material"; no loss stated. Letter §6 admits ~1,240 records, scope and access unknown, notification question unresolved.
- Buyer wants: Pre-Completion completion of investigation with report delivered; Seller-funded legal/forensic assessment of Privacy Act notifiable data breach (NDB) obligations; specific indemnity (outside cap/basket/time limit, or separate cap) for all costs, OAIC penalties, notification costs, third-party claims and remediation; warranty on data handling; update disclosure right only on Buyer consent.
- Recommendation: Specific uncapped indemnity plus pre-Completion investigation deliverable. *Reason: an unresolved NDB-scheme question with 1,240 individuals' data is a regulatory and reputational risk the Seller cannot responsibly characterise as "not material".*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- Seller: Three AUD 110k renewals (AUD 330k) are ordinary-course. Letter §8 admits silence on whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued.
- Buyer wants: Clarification of terms (term, termination rights, timing); if committed pre-Completion and benefit falls post-Completion, treat as ordinary course only if accrued in working capital; if they are a single arrangement split into three to avoid consent/materiality thresholds, treat as Leakage or price adjustment; Seller covenant not to renew without consent in the gap period.
- Recommendation: Request DD-008/011 detail and make the renewals subject to Buyer consent under gap controls. *Reason: three identical AUD 110k contracts "read together" suggests threshold-splitting, and unterminable commitments entered pre-Completion are Seller-side cost.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- Seller: Single regime – all limitations apply to all Claims unless stated.
- Buyer wants: Four distinct regimes: (i) general warranties (cap/basket/24 months); (ii) fundamental/title (100%, 6–7 years); (iii) tax (100%, 7 years); (iv) specific indemnities (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, privacy, Sandbar/leakage) – uncapped or separately capped, no basket, no knowledge or disclosure qualification.
- Recommendation: Insist on a limitation schedule with a category-by-category matrix. *Reason: the "applies to all Claims" default would collapse the specific indemnities into the AUD 4.8m general cap, defeating their purpose.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- Seller: Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Letter §10 disclaims that Buyer has verified.
- Buyer wants: Independent verification before signing – ASIC company extract, PPSR search against Company and Seller, constitution (pre-emption/transfer restrictions), share certificates, board minutes approving transfer, absence of options/convertibles; unqualified title warranty and Completion deliverables (executed transfers, certificates, register update).
- Recommendation: Run searches now; do not accept the register alone. *Reason: a share register is maintained by the Seller-controlled Company and is not conclusive against unregistered encumbrances or defective issuances.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms**
- Seller: "Settled under the general regime" (i.e. 20% cap, 18 months).
- Buyer wants: Standalone tax indemnity (pre-Completion tax, covenant-style, 100% cap, 7 years, no basket, no disclosure/knowledge qualification); full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source, employee/contractor assignments) with elevated cap (50–100%) and 3–6 years; these not "settled" by any general regime statement.
- Recommendation: Reject; table separate tax indemnity and IP warranty schedule. *Reason: for a SaaS business IP and tax are the core value and the longest-tail risks – they cannot sit under an 18-month, 20% regime.*

---

**Suggested priority order for the mark-up:** (1) Riverlark at Completion, (2) Bluefen CP, (3) fraud carve-out and category separation, (4) specific indemnities (privacy, Ironquay, bonuses), (5) cap/basket/time limits, (6) disclosure and knowledge, (7) tax/IP schedules and title searches. Items (1)–(4) are structural and should be flagged to the deal team as conditions of proceeding, not points for trading.
=== END ADVICE ===
